correctness.rationale: For closed intervals in nondecreasing right endpoint order, an earlier interval is disjoint from interval i exactly if its right endpoint is strictly less than the left endpoint of i. The earlier intervals eligible to accompany i thus form exactly the first k_i vertices (also with tied endpoints). Splitting independent sets by inclusion of i gives Z_i=Z_{i-1}+s_i Z_{k_i}. Choose each new sign to cancel the two terms if both are nonzero; induction from Z_0=1 keeps every prefix in {-1,0,1}. Every signed summand is odd, so this construction attains the least permitted magnitude, including for the empty graph. Walsh characters diagonalize the unnormalized convolution; the maximum magnitude is the unsigned count and the unit minimum in the invertible case gives the claimed norm and condition number. The sign scan is linear with predecessors given; sorting and strict predecessor searches take O(n log n). For the path power, [i,i+h] realizes the required edges and gives the stated predecessor index. For K_{2,2,2}, a nonempty independent set stays in one part, so the multiplier is 4t-2 where t counts parts having both signs positive; each other part has three sign patterns. This yields the claimed spectrum, and two parts induce a 4-cycle, outside interval graphs.
residual_risks: The bounded enumeration covers the obstruction only; the universal conclusion follows from the induction, not from the frozen recorded test output.

value.rationale: The minimum multiplier decides whether exact recovery is possible and, when it is, gives its sharp spectral conditioning. The predecessor-based construction supplies a uniform, efficiently findable witness across arbitrary interval graphs, replacing special-purpose periodic signings. The even-count invertible octahedron isolates why the easy general parity argument cannot give the converse without structure.
residual_risks: No claim about higher-dimensional graph classes or singular-case projection norms follows.
